![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/401368d830825a55e27fc6ba191a1c3dbb80d93b2e0af74db3337523817d2c65.png)

The region enclosed by the curve $y=\dfrac 3 2x+\dfrac 1 2,$ for $x\in [1,3],$ and the horizontal line $y=1$ is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the line $y=1,$ as shown above. Find an integral that represents the volume of the resulting solid.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that we are given that the limits of integration are from $x=1$ to $x=3$ along the $x$-axis. 

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/0434e16502f9b20bb53f3c46ba265239c59e8f5a487cdf3e71962fc0019a927d.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=1,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=\dfrac 3 2x+\dfrac 1 2.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{3}{[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{3}{[\,(\frac{3}{2}x+\frac{1}{2})-(1)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{3}{(\frac{3}{2}x-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
